title: CBSE CLASS 11 — English | Subject Verb Agreement
description: Subject-wise test on Subject Verb Agreement (English) for CBSE CLASS 11. 50Q.
subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The committee members ________ discussing the new proposal.

options.explanation: Incorrect: 'is' is a singular verb.
Incorrect: 'has' is a singular verb.
Incorrect: 'was' is a singular verb.
Correct: 'are' is the plural verb needed for the plural subject 'members'.

questions.explanation: The subject 'members' is plural, therefore it requires a plural verb 'are'.
questions.hint: Identify the subject and its number (singular/plural).
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Neither John nor Mary ________ present at the meeting yesterday.

options.explanation: Incorrect: 'were' is a plural verb.
Correct: 'was' is the singular verb needed for the singular subject 'Mary'.
Incorrect: 'are' is a plural verb.
Incorrect: 'have been' is a plural verb.

questions.explanation: When two singular subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. In this case, 'Mary' is singular, so the verb must be singular ('was').
questions.hint: Use the rule for subjects joined by 'neither...nor' to determine the correct verb.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The whole class ________ excited about the upcoming field trip to the museum.

options.explanation: Incorrect: 'were' is a plural verb.
Correct: 'was' is the singular verb needed for the singular subject 'class'.
Incorrect: 'are' is a plural verb.
Incorrect: 'have been' is a plural verb.

questions.explanation: 'Class' is a collective noun acting as a single, unified unit in this context, hence it takes a singular verb ('was').
questions.hint: Collective nouns can take singular or plural verbs depending on whether they are acting as a single unit or as individuals.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Bread and butter ________ his favourite breakfast, especially when served with a hot cup of tea.

options.explanation: Incorrect: 'are' is a plural verb.
Incorrect: 'were' is a plural verb.
Correct: 'is' is the singular verb needed for the singular subject 'bread and butter'.
Incorrect: 'have been' is a plural verb.

questions.explanation: 'Bread and butter' is a compound subject that refers to a single dish or idea (a single breakfast item), not two separate items. Therefore, it takes a singular verb ('is').
questions.hint: Compound subjects can take singular verbs if they refer to a single idea or item.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: The principal, as well as the teachers, ________ concerned about the students' declining performance.

options.explanation: Incorrect: 'are' is a plural verb.
Incorrect: 'were' is a plural verb.
Correct: 'is' is the singular verb needed for the singular subject 'principal'.
Incorrect: 'have been' is a plural verb.

questions.explanation: When a subject is followed by phrases like 'as well as,' 'along with,' 'together with,' 'in addition to,' the verb agrees with the *first* subject ('principal'), which is singular.
questions.hint: Phrases like 'as well as' do not affect the number of the subject; the verb agrees with the main subject.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Each of the students ________ submitted their project on time, which impressed the faculty.

options.explanation: Incorrect: 'have' is a plural verb.
Correct: 'has' is the singular verb needed for the singular subject 'each'.
Incorrect: 'were' is a plural verb.
Incorrect: 'are' is a plural verb.

questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns like 'each,' 'every,' 'everyone,' 'no one,' 'anybody' always take a singular verb.
questions.hint: Indefinite pronouns are always singular and require singular verbs.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: A number of volunteers ________ working tirelessly for the cause, but the number of donations received ________ still insufficient.

options.explanation: Incorrect: 'is' is singular, but 'a number of' requires a plural verb.
Incorrect: 'were' is plural, but 'the number of' requires a singular verb.
Correct: 'are' for the plural subject 'a number of volunteers' and 'is' for the singular subject 'the number of donations'.
Incorrect: 'is' is singular, but 'a number of' requires a plural verb.

questions.explanation: 'A number of' (meaning 'many') takes a plural verb ('are working'). 'The number of' (referring to a specific quantity) takes a singular verb ('is insufficient').
questions.hint: Distinguish between 'a number of' (always plural) and 'the number of' (always singular).
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sentence 'Physics are my most challenging subject' is grammatically incorrect. Reason (R): Nouns that appear plural in form but refer to a single subject, disease, or entity (e.g., mathematics, measles, news) always take a singular verb.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct: Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect: The reason explains the assertion correctly.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Both the assertion and the reason are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect: The assertion is true.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true because 'Physics are' is incorrect; it should be 'Physics is'. Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains the grammatical rule for subjects like 'physics'.
questions.hint: Recall the rule for nouns ending in '-ics' that refer to single subjects or disciplines.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Read the passage and fill in the blanks with the correct form of the verb: The recent changes in the school curriculum ________ (i) significant. Neither the teachers nor the principal ________ (ii) fully satisfied with the implementation, although the majority of students ________ (iii) adapted well. Every single one of the new guidelines ________ (iv) designed to improve learning outcomes.

options.explanation: Incorrect: The sequence does not match the subject-verb agreement rules.
Incorrect: The sequence does not match the subject-verb agreement rules.
Incorrect: The sequence does not match the subject-verb agreement rules.
Correct: The sequence '(i) are, (ii) is, (iii) have' matches the subject-verb agreement rules for the given passage.

questions.explanation: The sequence of verbs that correctly fills the blanks is: (i) 'are' (plural subject 'changes'), (ii) 'is' (subject closer to the verb is 'principal'), (iii) 'have' (plural subject 'majority of students'), (iv) 'was' (singular subject 'one of the new guidelines').
questions.hint: Pay attention to the subject-verb agreement rules for each blank.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence: 'The new principal, along with the teachers, ______ planning an orientation session for the freshers.'

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'are' is a plural verb and the main subject (principal) is singular.
Correct because the main subject 'principal' is singular and requires a singular verb 'is'.
Incorrect because 'were' is a plural past tense verb and does not agree with the singular subject.
Incorrect because 'have been' is a plural verb and the subject is singular.

questions.explanation: When a subject is followed by phrases like 'along with,' the verb agrees with the main subject (the principal), which is singular.
questions.hint: Identify the main subject of the sentence.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Identify the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:

options.text: Each of the participants were asked to submit their forms.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'Each' is singular and requires 'was asked'.

options.text: Neither the students nor the teacher are aware of the changes.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'Neither...nor' takes a verb that agrees with the subject closest to it ('the teacher' is singular, so 'is aware').

options.text: The committee has decided to postpone the meeting until next week.
options.explanation: Correct because 'The committee' acting as a single unit requires a singular verb 'has decided'.

options.text: A number of significant issues was discussed at the conference.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'A number of' takes a plural verb 'were discussed'.

questions.explanation: The correct sentence is the one where the subject and verb agree in number. 'The committee' acting as a single unit requires a singular verb.
questions.hint: Check for subject-verb agreement in each option.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the appropriate verb: 'Bread and butter ______ considered a wholesome breakfast by many.'

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'are' is a plural verb and 'bread and butter' is treated as a single unit here.
Correct because 'bread and butter' is considered a single dish or meal item, requiring a singular verb 'is'.
Incorrect because 'were' is a plural past tense verb and does not agree with the singular subject.
Incorrect because 'have been' is a plural verb and the subject is singular.

questions.explanation: When two singular subjects connected by 'and' refer to a single unit or idea, the verb used is singular.
questions.hint: Consider whether 'bread and butter' is treated as a single unit or separate items.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly applies the rule of Subject-Verb Agreement for indefinite pronouns?

options.text: Many of the students has submitted their projects.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'Many' is plural and requires 'have submitted'.

options.text: Everyone in the class is expected to participate in the debate.
options.explanation: Correct because 'Everyone' is a singular indefinite pronoun and requires the singular verb 'is'.

options.text: Several of the books was damaged in the flood.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'Several' is plural and requires 'were damaged'.

options.text: None of the options seems correct.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'None' can be singular or plural, but 'seems' is singular, making this option ambiguous and incorrect.

questions.explanation: Indefinite pronouns like 'everyone' are always singular and require a singular verb.
questions.hint: Identify the indefinite pronoun and its required verb form.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Choose the correct option for the blank: 'Neither the captain nor the players ______ happy with the referee's decision.'

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'was' is singular and does not agree with the plural subject 'players'.
Correct because 'players' is plural, and the verb 'were' agrees with it.
Incorrect because 'is' is singular and does not agree with the plural subject.
Incorrect because 'has been' is singular and does not agree with the plural subject.

questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'neither...nor,' the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Here, 'the players' (plural) is closer, so the plural verb 'were' is used.
questions.hint: The verb agrees with the subject nearest to it in 'neither...nor' constructions.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb: 'The number of accidents on this highway ______ significantly increased over the past year.'

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'are' is a plural verb and 'The number of' is singular.
Incorrect because 'have' is a plural verb and 'The number of' is singular.
Correct because 'The number of' is singular and requires the singular verb 'has'.
Incorrect because 'were' is a plural past tense verb and does not agree with the singular subject.

questions.explanation: 'The number of' is always treated as a singular subject, regardless of the noun that follows it, and requires a singular verb.
questions.hint: Remember that 'The number of' is always singular.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Select the sentence that demonstrates correct subject-verb agreement.

options.text: The quality of the products were not up to the mark.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'The quality' is the subject (singular) and requires 'was not'.

options.text: My spectacles is missing from the table.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'spectacles' is a plural noun and requires 'are missing'.

options.text: Politics is often considered a complex and challenging field.
options.explanation: Correct because 'Politics' as a field of study is singular and requires the singular verb 'is'.

options.text: All of the information are confidential.
options.explanation: Incorrect because 'information' is an uncountable noun and is always singular ('is confidential').

questions.explanation: Nouns ending in '-ics' such as 'politics' are usually singular when referring to a field of study or general concept.
questions.hint: Consider whether the subject is a field of study or a general concept.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Fill in the blank appropriately: 'The manager, as well as his team members, ______ working late to meet the deadline.'

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'are' is a plural verb and does not agree with the singular subject.
Correct because the main subject 'manager' is singular and requires the singular verb 'is'.
Incorrect because 'were' is a plural past tense verb and does not agree with the singular subject.
Incorrect because 'have' is a plural verb and does not agree with the singular subject.

questions.explanation: When a singular subject is connected to another noun by 'as well as,' the verb agrees with the main subject, which is singular.
questions.hint: The main subject is 'The manager,' which is singular.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): The sentence 'The United States are a powerful nation' is grammatically incorrect. Reason (R): Country names that are plural in form but refer to a single entity take a singular verb.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Correct because both A and R are true, and R directly explains why A is incorrect.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: Incorrect because R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: Incorrect because both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: Incorrect because A is true.

questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is true because the sentence should use 'is' instead of 'are.' Reason (R) is true and correctly explains why A is incorrect, as 'The United States' is a single entity and requires a singular verb.
questions.hint: Consider the grammatical rules for country names and subject-verb agreement.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Read the following passage and identify the sentence that contains an error in Subject-Verb Agreement: (1) The new policy regarding student attendance is quite strict. (2) Each of the teachers have been informed about its implementation. (3) A majority of the students feel that the rules are too rigid. (4) However, the school management believes that it will improve discipline.

options.explanation: Incorrect because 'The new policy' is singular and correctly uses 'is'.
Correct because 'Each' is singular and should use 'has' instead of 'have'.
Incorrect because 'A majority of the students' is plural and correctly uses 'feel'.
Incorrect because 'the school management' is singular and correctly uses 'believes'.

questions.explanation: Sentence (2) contains the error because 'Each' is a singular indefinite pronoun and requires a singular verb 'has' instead of 'have.'
questions.hint: Look for subject-verb agreement errors in the passage.
questions.subject: cbse11-english

questions.question: Identify the correct sentence where the subject and verb agree in number.

options.text: The list of items are on the desk.
options.explanation: The verb 'are' is plural, but the subject 'list' is singular.

options.text: The list of items is on the desk.
options.explanation: The verb 'is' is singular, matching the singular subject 'list'.

options.text: The list of items has been on the desk.
options.explanation: The verb 'has been' is singular, but the structure is unnecessarily complex for the sentence.

options.text: The list of items have been on the desk.
options.explanation: The verb 'have been' is plural, but the subject 'list' is singular.

questions.explanation: The subject 'list' is singular, so it must take the singular verb 'is.' The other options incorrectly use plural verbs ('are,' 'have been') with a singular subject.
questions.hint: The subject 'list' is singular, so the verb must also be singular.
